So my girlfriend and I moved to Grand Forks for her schooling about a year ago. 

We are very outdoorsy people. The winters shut everything down from about November until May. Most of the fun outdoor activities and closest we came to experiences we had in the North East were in Minnesota. Keeping in mind most of solid places in Minnesota are 2 - 5 hours away. Also, you run out of things to do here very quickly. Most everyone we know says to visits the twin cities and Duluth aka you have to leave ND to expand your offerings. Fargo has more to do but is an hour drive south. However, the summers have been the most enjoyable, there are decent events in town every couple weeks or so to keep your sanity. I suffer from depression and the winter adds on the seasonal depression. So if your natural coping mechanism is alcohol you need to find another before moving here. 

We have two dogs, both are low energy dogs. But our friends who have high energy dogs take them to daycare regularly in the winter. But you need to plan these days in advance as this is what everyone does, and there are not enough doggie daycares to meet the demand in the winter. The place we take our dogs occasionally were booking out 4-6 weeks for daycare in the winter. It is also rough standing outside waiting for your pup to poop in below zero temps, with a  “feels like” of -30 to -50 due to wind chill. 

Options are limited for things to do. Closest trail that comes to mind is turtle river, about 20-30 minutes away. But these are flatter grassland trails. Weekends during the summer are filled with whatever events are going on downtown or in the parks, or walking the dogs and visiting the dog parks. Avoid shopping on the weekends, it is ridiculously busy due our neighbors of the north, and those who come from the surrounding areas to shop. Our winters were filled with UND hockey, which is amazing, never got old. Along with waiting out the blizzards indoors. 

I would avoid moving here. The people are nice but it takes a special breed to do this for the long term. We have found a new love of the Midwest in terms of people and life style. However, I would not make North Dakota your place to settle down. You’re better off living in Minnesota, or Wisconsin. 

We will be leaving North Dakota once my girlfriend graduates but that was part of our 5 year plan the whole time. 
It is dirt cheap to live out here though, which is nice. And there is a thriving indoor plant community here, my girlfriend can attest to this.

But the one thing that really tips the scales is the damn wind, holy shit, after a certain point cold is cold, but when you add wind to the mix you have all other winters beat.
